pulls.title: Address review findings in protocol text
pulls.author: masa-koz
pulls.body:
Fixes the issues found by a review of the -00 text before submission.

## Protocol fixes
- **Amplification (§Limits, §Security):** at most one punch packet per *received packet*, however many PUNCH_ME_NOW frames it carries. Clients SHOULD send each request in its own packet. The rate limit is now a MUST. This closes off packet-count amplification and the saved-up byte budget released as a burst.
- **Request forgery (§Limits, §Security):** SHOULD NOT punch toward loopback, link-local or internal-only addresses. The server MAY refuse sensitive ports, following RFC 9000 §21.5.6.
- **Multipath Path IDs (§Validation):** abandoned Path IDs can't be reused, so each attempt uses one up for good. The server SHOULD raise MAX_PATH_ID, and the client can send PATHS_BLOCKED. The appendix comparison is updated to match.
- **Header protection (§Punch Packets):** a 1-RTT punch packet MUST be long enough for the header-protection sample (RFC 9001 §5.4.2).
- **Packet number (§Punch Packets):** says which packet number space to use (per path under multipath), and the number is consumed so the AEAD nonce is never reused.

## Clarifications
- Intro property reworded. New text in §Migration: the server validates the client's address on migration (RFC 9000 §9.3), which can add one round trip.
- The "exactly one sending base per address" claim is softened to match Open Issues.
- Clients using zero-length connection IDs are covered (the packet fails authentication; this counts toward the integrity limit).
- The Stateless Reset size statement is corrected (RFC 9000 §10.3 / §10.3.3).
- Added an RFC 9001 reference.
- CODEOWNERS now uses `@masa-koz` instead of an email that may not be verified. Note: `make update-codeowners` will regenerate it from the draft's author email.

## Not changed
The Implementation Status section still says the SEERA punch packet is sent "without padding". Please confirm whether the implementation meets the header-protection minimum, and update that text or the "Differences" list.

The draft was not built locally. Please check the CI build of this PR.

pulls.title: Fix BCP 14 boilerplate for mmark
pulls.author: masa-koz
pulls.body:
`{::boilerplate bcp14-tagged}` is kramdown-rfc syntax. mmark doesn't process it, so the published draft showed it as literal text in Section 2. The BCP 14 key-words paragraph and the RFC 2119/8174 references were missing as a result.

- Replace the directive with the standard RFC 8174 key-words paragraph, citing `[@!RFC2119] [@!RFC8174]`.
- Add `<reference>` entries for RFC 2119 and RFC 8174, matching the existing explicit references.

No other kramdown-only syntax was found. The rendered text has no other leftover `{...}` markup.

pulls.title: Cite RFC 10069 for QUIC multipath
pulls.author: masa-koz
pulls.body:
QUIC multipath has been published as [RFC 10069](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc10069) (Proposed Standard, November 2026).

- Replace every `[@!I-D.ietf-quic-multipath]` with `[@!RFC10069]`, and swap the draft-21 `<reference>` for an RFC 10069 entry. The entry uses the RFC's author list with editor roles and DOI `10.17487/RFC10069`.
- Add section citations to the multipath text:
  - Path IDs are never reused after abandonment: RFC 10069 §3.4
  - MAX_PATH_ID: §4.6
  - PATHS_BLOCKED: §4.7

The RFC still has the PATH_ABANDON, MAX_PATH_ID and PATHS_BLOCKED frames and the rule against reusing path IDs. The draft's multipath text needed no other changes.
